paper.title: LOGOS: A Living Logic for AI Agent Teams That Evolve With Humans

related_fujitsu_page.scope: public technology description only; not an executable gate/ledger artifact

verified_primary_facts: The paper explicitly separates self-evolution data into proposal, optional candidate-selection, final-gate, and report sets. For K>1 candidates, a separate selection split chooses the candidate and a final gate split not used for selection decides acceptance.
The paper explicitly states that reported before/after numbers use a third report holdout not used for proposal, selection, or adoption.

The optional anytime-valid gate requires the proposal and candidate-selection rule to be fixed before the final gate stream begins; final-gate examples and per-example failures must remain hidden from the proposer; paired differences must be bounded or normalized; and bets must be predictable from past gate information only.

The paper explicitly limits sequential validity to fresh i.i.d. gate samples, replacement sampling from a fixed gate pool, or a fixed-sample evaluation without a sequential claim; reading a finite holdout without replacement is stated not to satisfy the streaming conditional-mean null by itself.

The adoption rule uses gain, regression and optional safety streams with an intersection-union composite p-value, and routes candidate decisions through a LORD-style alpha-wealth ledger. Formal LORD++ semantics are conditional on super-uniform candidate p-values, predictable spending and the stated dependence assumptions; otherwise the ledger is only conservative audit accounting.

Each final gate exposes a proposal-safe view containing decision, aggregate counts, score deltas and hashes while withholding task identifiers and per-example failures. The paper explicitly acknowledges repeated aggregate feedback as a leakage channel and defines a gate-exposure budget over max decisions, max aggregate releases and max cumulative privacy loss.

The common-candidate replay reports 2,500 deterministic decisions (500 seeds x five candidate families): no gate harmful adoption 0.600, paired gate harmful adoption 0.000 with adoption 0.200, and anytime-valid gate harmful adoption 0.000 with adoption 0.198. The paper labels this a gate-semantics mechanism check, not evidence about proposal quality in the wild.

The larger 5,000-decision robustness replay preserves the qualitative ordering under the same constructed candidate-family setup; the paper explicitly treats it as a semantic robustness check rather than an independent external benchmark.

The multi-seed HotpotQA/MATH-500 anytime-valid rows report zero report-holdout regressions because the anytime-valid gate fully rejects in those low-signal cells; the paper explicitly frames this as conservative error-accounted behavior rather than high adoption power.

The paper's gpt-4o-mini complementary view uses n=20 report holdout, proposal/gate budget 28 and seed 0; K=1 selected candidates are beneficial or neutral on the report holdout, while paired K=3 rejects the selected MATH-500 candidate.

scope_corrections.claim: LOGOS provides executable evidence that OUTER/report data are never queried by rollback, routing, stopping, recovery, or hidden orchestration before terminal reporting.
scope_corrections.reason: The paper contract excludes report-holdout use for proposal, selection, or adoption, but the checked primary paper does not establish a public executable zero-query proof across every other control path. The clean worker already flagged this stronger requirement as only partially verified.

scope_corrections.claim: The anytime-valid CERTIFY guarantee applies to ordinary finite holdout reads without replacement.
scope_corrections.reason: Appendix D.1 explicitly says a fixed finite holdout read without replacement does not by itself satisfy the i.i.d. conditional-mean null used for the sequential claim. The guarantee requires the stated streaming/replacement assumptions or a fixed-sample analysis with no sequential claim.

scope_corrections.claim: The LORD ledger automatically gives formal FDR control merely because candidate-level p-values are emitted.
scope_corrections.reason: The paper conditions formal LORD++ semantics on conditionally super-uniform candidate p-values, predictable spending and dependence assumptions; otherwise it calls the ledger conservative audit accounting.

scope_corrections.claim: Zero harmful adoption in the 2,500/5,000 decision replays estimates real-world harmful-proposal prevalence or natural proposal quality.
scope_corrections.reason: Both are constructed common-candidate mechanism replays; the paper explicitly rejects population interpretation over naturally occurring proposals.

scope_corrections.claim: A public executable LOGOS/MAAF implementation was verified in this audit.
scope_corrections.reason: The checked primary paper and Fujitsu technology page establish the protocol and related product-level description, but no source-bound executable gate/ledger implementation was verified in this run. Bounded public search non-discovery is not proof of absence.

safe_to_use: LOGOS is direct paper-level evidence for an EXPLORE/proposal -> optional TUNE/selection -> disjoint final CERTIFY -> separate report/OUTER composition.
The anytime-valid certification layer has an explicit sampler/filtration contract and does not license sequential reuse of an ordinary finite holdout without replacement.
The paper treats certification feedback itself as an adaptive information channel and budgets aggregate releases/exposure.
Cross-candidate online error accounting is only formal when candidate-level validity and spending/dependence assumptions are actually satisfied.
do_not_promote_without_more_evidence: Crash-safe persistence or restart semantics of the candidate-level e-process/LORD ledger.
Executable proof that report/OUTER data are unused by routing, rollback, stopping, recovery or hidden scripts before terminal reporting.
Paper-run replay or implementation correctness without a source-bound public executable artifact.
Natural proposal-quality or production-safety rates from the constructed 2,500/5,000 decision replays.

exact_next_verification: Rotate to another C28 sealed namespace with source-bound primary code or raw quantitative artifact. Prefer a claim where direct recomputation can change evidence status. Do not revisit LOGOS unless a public executable implementation, paper artifact bundle, or exact run ledger becomes available. Never write exploration-worker state or feedback.
